segments.text: What if I told you winning the toss barely improves your chances of winning an IPL match?
Sounds unbelievable?
Let's look at the numbers.
Across thousands of matches, toss winners won fifty-four percent of decided Tests,
forty-nine point six percent of ODIs,
fifty point three percent of T20 internationals,
and fifty-one point six percent in the IPL.
Now imagine you're the captain.
It's an IPL match under lights.
There's a chance of dew later.
You win the toss.
Would you bat first, or bowl first?
In this IPL dataset, captains who chose to bowl first won nearly fifty-five percent.
Those who chose to bat won just forty-five percent.
But that doesn't mean bowling first is always better.
But wait.
In {2024,|twenty twenty-four,} IPL toss winners won only forty-four percent of matches.
In {2025,|twenty twenty-five,} that jumped to sixty-one percent.
The coin didn't change.
So what did?
Here's where the science gets interesting.
Researchers found almost no average toss advantage in daytime international limited-overs cricket.
But in day-night matches, the estimated advantage rose by three point three percentage points.
In Test cricket, the estimated toss advantage was even larger, around four point nine percentage points.
And over five days, the pitch itself can become a completely different surface.
So the real advantage isn't simply winning a coin flip.
It's having the choice.
And the value of that choice changes with the pitch, weather, match format and conditions.
So, does winning the toss win matches?
Usually, not by much.
But in the right conditions, that small coin can make a meaningful difference.
The toss starts the match.
It doesn't decide the winner.
Beyond The Scoreboard.
